pos.personaBrief: Benitez's Liverpool sat in two banks of four vs Chelsea, were comfortable in a low block vs Milan and attacked on the counter; Chelsea dominated possession in the tie they won.

pro.personaBrief: Liverpool used long clearances to Cisse on the break and quick first-time passing against Chelsea, with a crammed midfield; slow build-up vs Milan's press.

est.personaBrief: A drilled system with set positions that players took long to learn (Warnock); strikers stayed central and Garcia drifting infield was criticised as lacking width.

lar.personaBrief: Riise crosses and full-backs stretching Milan were outlets, but the side was built on a crammed five-man central midfield and Gerrard/Alonso in the middle.

blo.personaBrief: Two lines of four within 40 yards of goal vs Chelsea, low block vs Milan and 5-3-1-1 vs Juventus; harrying in bursts but no sustained high press.

mar.personaBrief: Benitez's zonal marking at set pieces, kept despite criticism, with player-specific tasks such as Gerrard on Serginho and 5-3-1-1 to contain Juventus stars.

pla.personaBrief: Dropped the Valencia 4-2-3-1 for 4-4-2, used 5-3-1-1 vs Juventus, changed to three at the back at half-time in Istanbul and rotated heavily; strongly opponent-driven.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic: defensive containment vs Chelsea and Juventus, fifth in league while prioritising Europe; result over show.

sis.personaBrief: Benitez emphasised technical staff, preparation and role discipline; Gerrard and others had defined tasks; system over improvisation.

jog.personaBrief: Blend of Alonso and Garcia technique with Hamann, Carragher, Hyypia and Gerrard's drive; defensive duels and aerial strength mattered in big European ties.

bas.personaBrief: Built through signings (Alonso, Garcia, Morientes, Pellegrino); youth used mainly in cup rotation games.

lid.personaBrief: Benitez as a controlling, hands-on boss with technical staff; heavy rotation including stars and decisions his alone.
